questions.q: What is one trait that describes Anand’s attitude toward his inventions?
questions.a: Anand is curious or confident. A wrong answer like "he is a professional engineer" shows the student is confusing the character's hobby/self-image with his actual reality in the story.

questions.q: Why does the author describe Anand as "stubborn"?
questions.a: He is described as stubborn because he continues to work on his inventions even after they fail repeatedly. A wrong answer like "because he listens to his sister" shows the student has not understood the conflict in the story.

questions.q: If Anand’s invention fails, how would he likely react compared to a "practical" person?
questions.a: Anand would likely try to fix it or start a new version, while a practical person might stop to assess if the design is actually possible. If the student says "he would give up," they are failing to apply the trait of "confidence" mentioned in the text.

questions.q: How does the narrator's perspective highlight Anand’s naivety?
questions.a: The narrator (his sister) sees the flaws in the designs that Anand ignores, showing he lacks a realistic perspective. A student who misses this fails to see how the narrator serves as a foil to Anand.

questions.q: Is Anand’s persistence a positive or negative trait in this story? Justify your answer.
questions.a: It can be argued as positive (shows dedication) or negative (shows a lack of realism). The justification must cite his repeated failures vs. his refusal to stop. A wrong answer lacks evidence from the text.

questions.q: Describe a new invention Anand might make and how his traits (curiosity/stubbornness) would influence him.
questions.a: An answer should describe an imaginative but likely flawed machine and explain that Anand would keep tinkering with it despite others telling him it won't work. A poor answer ignores his specific personality traits.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Character analysis is the process of examining a character's traits, ______, and behaviors to understand their role and personality in a story.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever met someone who keeps ______ to build something, even if it falls apart every time?
What is Character analysis? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Character analysis is the process of examining a character's traits, motivations, and behaviors to understand their role and personality in a story.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Character analysis?
questions.a: Students often confuse "what a character does" with "who a character is." They might say "Anand is an inventor" instead of identifying the trait of "curiosity." This happens because they focus on the plot event rather than the underlying personality.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify at least three character traits of Anand and provide a specific example of an action or behavior from the text that supports each trait.
